- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.10), model overreacts to recent highs; apply mean reversion by subtracting 1–3% per day from forecast until sentiment shifts.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward overestimating early in the period; adjust downward by 3–8% for first 7–10 days if sentiment is weak.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.50 values (strong bullish), model often fails to account for eventual correction; add a 5–10% downward bias after 3 consecutive 0.50s.
- When true outcome shows sudden drop after spike, model often fails to recognize it; apply lag correction: if true price drops >5% from peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days.
